title: Cumulative frequency & IQR
examples: How do I find the median from a cumulative frequency graph?
What is the difference between a quartile and a percentile?
Can I estimate the IQR if I only have raw data?

explain.say: Today we will look at cumulative frequency graphs. These graphs help us see how data builds up.
The graph plots the running total of the data. The y axis shows the cumulative frequency count. The x axis shows the class boundaries.
To find a quartile, we use the percentage rule. For the first quartile, we look for the twenty-fifth percentile. This means we find the value corresponding to twenty-five percent of the total count.
The median, or second quartile, is always at the fifty percent mark. You find the value on the x axis where the cumulative frequency line crosses the fifty percent mark.
The third quartile is at the seventy-five percent mark. This value helps us estimate the spread of the middle fifty percent of our data.

faq.q: What is the interquartile range, or IQR?
faq.a: The IQR is the difference between the third quartile and the first quartile. It tells us the spread of the middle fifty percent of the data.
asks: How do I estimate the spread using quartiles?

faq.q: Do I need to know the total count to find the quartiles?
faq.a: Yes, you need the total count to find the correct percentages. The first quartile is always twenty-five percent of that total count.
asks: Is the total count important for percentiles?
Where do I find the percentage value?

faq.q: Can I just read the graph directly for the quartiles?
faq.a: You read the graph by finding the correct percentage mark on the y axis. Then you trace across to the curve and down to the x axis.
asks: How do I read the graph for the median?
Do I read the y axis or the x axis?

faq.q: What if the graph is not perfectly smooth?
faq.a: If the graph is not perfectly smooth, you must estimate carefully. Use the grid lines to make your best visual guess for the value.
asks: What if the points are scattered?
How accurate do I need to be?

faq.q: Is the IQR the same as the range?
faq.a: No, the range is just the difference between the maximum and minimum values. The IQR is more resistant to extreme outliers.
asks: What is the difference between range and IQR?
Which measure is better if there are weird numbers?

facts: The first quartile, Q1, marks the twenty-fifth percentile.
The median, or Q2, marks the fifty-percentile.
The third quartile, Q3, marks the seventy-five-percentile.
The Interquartile Range is calculated as Q3 minus Q1.

quiz.say: If the total count is one hundred, what percentage does the first quartile represent?
quiz.why: The first quartile is defined as the twenty-fifth percentile mark.

wrong.1: This is the value for the median, which is the second quartile.
wrong.2: This represents the total count, not the first quartile.
wrong.3: This is the value for the third quartile, not the first.

quiz.say: A student reads the graph and finds Q3 is twenty and Q1 is ten. What is the IQR?
quiz.why: You subtract the first quartile value from the third quartile value.

wrong.0: This is the sum of the two quartiles, not the difference.
wrong.1: This is only the value of the third quartile, ignoring Q1.
wrong.2: You cannot find the difference by subtracting a number from itself.

quiz.say: If the median is found at the value of fifteen, what percentage of the data is below this point?
quiz.why: The median always divides the data into two equal halves, representing fifty percent.

wrong.1: This is the percentage associated with the first quartile.
wrong.2: This is the percentage associated with the third quartile.
wrong.3: This represents the entire dataset, not just the lower half.
